title: Nectar replenishment maintains the neutral effects of nectar robbing on female reproductive success of Salvia przewalskii (Lamiaceae), a plant pollinated and robbed by bumble bees
decision_basis: Primary study treats robbed versus legitimately visited flowers as the exposure and tests nectar replenishment, legitimate-pollinator visitation and female reproductive success; it does not use access geometry as a predictor of robbery route use.

title: Variation in composition of two bumble bee species across communities affects nectar robbing but maintains pollinator visitation rate to an alpine plant, Salvia przewalskii
decision_basis: Across 26 communities, robbery incidence is modeled against bumble-bee relative abundance, floral diversity, plant population size and floral resource; tongue-length differences motivate species roles but are not the focal quantitative robbery predictor.
notes: Community-composition predictor, outside frozen access-geometry estimand.

title: Does pollination syndrome reflect pollinator efficiency in Silene nutans?
decision_basis: Primary study tests nocturnal versus diurnal pollination effectiveness and reproductive output under a pollination-syndrome question; no geometry-to-robbery route response is estimated.

title: Herbivory and Time Since Flowering Shape Floral Rewards and Pollinator-Pathogen Interactions
decision_basis: Primary experiment tests leaf-herbivory effects on nectar/pollen alkaloids and downstream bumblebee-pathogen infection; no route-resolved nectar-robbing outcome is analyzed.
notes: Chemical/reward and pathogen study outside direct geometry-route lane.

title: Nectar robbers deter legitimate pollinators by mutilating flowers
decision_basis: Study asks how robber-caused floral mutilation changes subsequent legitimate-pollinator visitation and reproduction; floral morphology is altered by robbery rather than an independent pre-existing geometry predictor of robbery.

title: Using ecological and field survey data to establish a national list of the wild bee pollinators of crops
decision_basis: National crop-pollinator synthesis combines ecological traits and flower-visitor surveys to identify pollinating bee species; it does not model legitimate versus nectar-robbing route use.

title: Landscape composition modifies pollinator densities, foraging behavior and yield formation in faba beans
decision_basis: Primary study records nectar robbing but models bee density/foraging behaviour against landscape composition such as faba-bean, oilseed-rape and semi-natural habitat cover; access geometry is not the robbery predictor.

title: Nectar robbing by bees on the flowers of Volkameria inermis (Lamiaceae) in Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary, Andhra Pradesh, India
decision_basis: Natural-history study documents nectar robbing on tubular flowers but does not estimate variation in an access-geometry predictor against robbery probability/frequency.
notes: Descriptive robbery biology without geometry-response estimate.

title: Interaction between Bombus terrestris and honeybees in red clover fields reduces abundance of other bumblebees and red clover yield
decision_basis: Empirical master's study manipulates/compares managed bee abundances and tests bee-community competition and red-clover yield; B. terrestris robbery is observed, but floral or visitor-flower access geometry is not the focal predictor.
notes: Primary empirical thesis is excluded by predictor mismatch rather than document status.

title: Nesting and Biology of Alastor mocsaryi (Hymenoptera, Vespidae: Eumeninae)
decision_basis: Study concerns nest structure and nesting biology of an eumenine wasp; no floral nectar-robbing route response is analyzed.

title: Flower selection of Xylocopa violacea: aromatic and ornamental plants as resources in a botanic garden
decision_basis: Conference paper analyzes plant-family/origin/flower-morphology preferences of Xylocopa violacea and notes that legitimate or illegitimate visits can occur, but does not provide a quantitative access-geometry predictor against robbery/illegitimate-route probability.
notes: Flower-selection study without direct geometry-to-route estimate.

title: Flower Morphology Influences Pollinator Community with Implications for Cross-Pollination: Observations in Rabbiteye Blueberry (Vaccinium ashei Reade)
decision_basis: Poster compares blueberry cultivar morphology and visitor-community composition; the reported response is pollinator-community/visitation structure rather than a route-resolved robbery outcome modeled against geometry.
notes: Morphology-to-community study, not formal geometry-to-robbery test.
